# Feature-server `/v2` API (outbound calls from Cognigy.AI)

## TL;DR

- `/v2` is how a linked Cognigy.AI cluster's `vg-runtime-api` asks this VG cluster to place a call. Design: `vg-resources` `docs/tdd/06-vg-in-ai/006-outbound-call-ai-authentication.md` §6–§7.
- Off by default (`featureServer.v2Api.enabled: false`). `POST /v2/createCall` answers `501` until outbound runtime resolution (006 G5) lands.
- Auth is a per-request ES256 JWT from the AI cluster, verified by feature-server against that AI cluster's JWKS. There are no shared secrets and nothing to seal.
- The chart publishes `/v2/` only. `/v1` and `/health` stay internal.

## How the link works

```
AI cluster                                     VG cluster (this chart)
vg-runtime-api ──POST /v2/createCall──▶ Traefik (/v2/ only, body + rate limit) ──▶ feature-server
   signs: iss=<AI name> aud=<VG name>                verifies: iss ∈ AI_CLUSTER_TRUST_LIST,
          jti, bdh=sha256(body)                                aud = VG_CLUSTER_NAME,
   /vg/runtime/.well-known/jwks.json ◀── fetched every 5 min ── jti single-use (Redis), body hash
```

`resourceResolver.runtimeApiTargets` already lists the linked AI clusters for the opposite direction (019). The same list now feeds feature-server, so a link is configured once:

| Target field | VG → AI (resolver) | AI → VG (feature-server `/v2`) |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | JWT `aud` | expected JWT `iss` |
| `url` | resolve calls | default JWKS base |
| `jwksUrl` (new, optional) | — | AI cluster's JWKS. Default: `<url without trailing /v1>/.well-known/jwks.json` |

## Hostname and routing (no new DNS entry)

`/v2` is served on the existing API hostname (`ingress.api.host`), the same one api-server uses. It is split by path, not by host:

| Ingress | Host | Path | Backend |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api-server` | `ingress.api.host` | `/` (Prefix) | `api-server` |
| `feature-server-v2` | `ingress.api.host` (or `v2Api.ingress.host`) | `/v2/` (Prefix) | `feature-server-headless:<ports.tcp>` |

Traefik picks the longest matching rule, so `/v2/...` goes straight to feature-server and never touches api-server. Everything else on that host, including `/v1`, still goes to api-server. Feature-server's own `/v1` stays unreachable from outside.

The backend is the headless Service, so Traefik connects to the pod IPs directly (bypassing kube-proxy). With the NetworkPolicy enabled, the Traefik pods must therefore be allowed to reach the HTTP port; see below.

For SRE:
- **DNS and TLS:** nothing new while `v2Api.ingress.host` is empty; the existing record and certificate cover `/v2/`. Setting `v2Api.ingress.host` introduces a separate hostname, which needs its own DNS record and a certificate that covers it. The chart creates neither.
- **Reachability:** the API host must be reachable from the AI cluster's egress addresses. The rate limit is per source IP, so any WAF or load balancer in front must forward the real client IP.

## Values

```yaml
vgCluster:
  name: vg-prod-eu            # set explicitly on a linked cluster; it is the /v2 `aud`
resourceResolver:
  runtimeApiTargets:
    - name: ai-prod-eu        # must equal the AI side's vgRuntimeApi.clusterName
      url: https://api-eu.cognigy.ai/vg/runtime
featureServer:
  v2Api:
    enabled: true
    ingress:
      enabled: true           # host defaults to ingress.api.host
      rateLimit: { average: 50, burst: 100 }   # per source IP
      maxRequestBodyBytes: 16384
    networkPolicy:
      enabled: false          # opt-in, see below
```

The AI side additionally needs `vgRuntimeApi.auth.clusters.<vgCluster.name>.callControlUrl: https://<ingress.api.host>` (vg-domain `charts/vg-agentic`).

## What renders

| Object | When |
|---|---|
| feature-server env `VG_CLUSTER_NAME`, `AI_CLUSTER_TRUST_LIST` (JSON) | `v2Api.enabled` and at least one target |
| Ingress `feature-server-v2` (`/v2/` → `feature-server-headless:3000`), Middlewares `feature-server-v2-body-limit`, `feature-server-v2-rate-limit` | the above and `ingress.enabled` and `v2Api.ingress.enabled` |
| NetworkPolicy `feature-server-v2-api` | the above and `v2Api.networkPolicy.enabled` |

Render-time failures:
- No resolvable or whitespace cluster name (`vg.clusterName.validate`).
- A plaintext JWKS URL outside loopback or in-cluster `*.svc` DNS.
- An ingress with no host.
- An ingress class other than Traefik.

## NetworkPolicy

Selecting the feature-server pods makes every ingress port default-deny, so the policy re-opens everything except the HTTP port:
- TCP `1..PORT-1` and `PORT+1..65535` from anywhere.
- UDP `1..65535` from anywhere.
- TCP `PORT` from this namespace only, which includes the bundled Traefik. Set `ingressControllerNamespace` for an external controller.

SCTP is closed; nothing in the pod uses it. Requires Kubernetes ≥ 1.25 (`endPort`).

## Rotation

The AI side rotates by publishing both public keys, waiting longer than 5 minutes, then retiring the old key. Feature-server refreshes every AI cluster's JWKS every 5 minutes and keeps the previous keys if a fetch fails. Nothing changes on this side.

## Rate limiting caveat

The ingress cannot read the JWT, so the limit is per source IP rather than per AI cluster (006 asks for per-`iss`). AI clusters egress from few NAT addresses, so size the limit for the busiest linked AI cluster.
